questions.q: What are the SI base units of force?
questions.why: F = ma, so N = kg × m s⁻².

questions.q: A length is measured as 2.50 ± 0.05 m. What is the percentage uncertainty?
Which pair contains one scalar and one vector?
questions.why: Work is a scalar; momentum is a vector.

questions.q: When two quantities are multiplied, their percentage uncertainties are…
questions.why: For products and quotients, add the percentage uncertainties.

questions.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at 2.0 m s⁻² for 5.0 s. How far does it go?
A ball is thrown horizontally off a cliff. Ignoring air resistance, its horizontal velocity…
questions.why: No horizontal force acts, so horizontal velocity is constant; only the vertical velocity changes.

questions.q: The gradient of a displacement–time graph gives…
questions.why: Velocity = rate of change of displacement.

questions.q: An object is dropped from rest. How fast is it moving after falling 20 m? (g = 9.81 m s⁻²)
A 0.50 kg ball hits a wall at 6.0 m s⁻¹ and rebounds at 4.0 m s⁻¹. What is the change in momentum?
questions.why: Δp = 0.50 × (4.0 − (−6.0)) = 5.0 N s, as the direction reverses.

questions.q: In a perfectly elastic collision, what is conserved besides momentum?
questions.why: Elastic means total kinetic energy is conserved; the relative speed of approach equals that of separation.

questions.q: Newton's second law states that resultant force equals…
o: the rate of change of momentum
questions.why: F = Δp/Δt, which becomes F = ma for constant mass.

questions.q: The pairs in Newton's third law act on…
questions.why: Third-law pairs are equal and opposite and act on different bodies.

questions.q: For an object in equilibrium, which is true?
o: The resultant force is zero only
The resultant moment is zero only
Both the resultant force and the resultant moment are zero
questions.why: Equilibrium needs no resultant force and no resultant torque.

questions.q: What is upthrust on a submerged object equal to?
questions.why: Archimedes' principle; it comes from the pressure difference across the object (ρgV).

questions.q: The torque of a couple equals…
o: one force × the perpendicular distance between the forces
questions.why: Two equal, opposite, parallel forces produce a torque F × d.

questions.q: A motor lifts a 20 kg load 3.0 m in 4.0 s. What is its useful power output? (g = 9.81)
Power can also be written as…
questions.why: P = W/t = F × (s/t) = Fv.

questions.q: A machine has 600 J input and 450 J useful output. Its efficiency is…
Young modulus is defined as…
questions.why: E = stress/strain, in Pa.

questions.q: What does the area under a force–extension graph (within the limit of proportionality) represent?
questions.why: Work done stretching it = ½Fx.

questions.q: Plastic deformation means the material…
o: does not return to its original shape when the load is removed
questions.why: Beyond the elastic limit, the deformation is permanent.

questions.q: Intensity of a wave is proportional to…
questions.why: Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared: I ∝ A².

questions.q: A source moves towards a stationary observer. The observed frequency is…
questions.why: Doppler effect: wavefronts bunch up, so the frequency observed is higher.

questions.q: Which waves can be polarised?
questions.why: Polarisation restricts oscillation to one plane, which needs transverse oscillations.

questions.q: Unpolarised light passes through a polariser, then an analyser at 60°. What fraction of the light after the polariser gets through? (Malus's law)
questions.why: I = I₀ cos²60° = 0.25 I₀.

questions.q: In a stationary wave, the distance between adjacent nodes is…
questions.why: Nodes are half a wavelength apart.

questions.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, fringe spacing x = λD/a. What happens if the slit separation a is halved?
questions.why: x is inversely proportional to a.

questions.q: A diffraction grating has 500 lines per mm. What is the line spacing d?
For a stable interference pattern, the sources must be…
questions.why: Coherent sources have a constant phase difference.

questions.q: A wire of length 2.0 m and cross-sectional area 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m² has resistivity 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m. What is its resistance?
In I = Anvq, what is v?
o: The mean drift velocity of the charge carriers
questions.why: n is the number density, A the area, q the charge, v the drift velocity.

questions.q: Power dissipated in a resistor can be written as…
questions.why: P = VI = I²R = V²/R.

questions.q: Kirchhoff's first law is a consequence of conservation of…
questions.why: Current into a junction equals current out: charge is conserved.

questions.q: A cell of e.m.f. 6.0 V and internal resistance 1.0 Ω is connected to a 5.0 Ω resistor. What is the current?
In a potential divider of 2 kΩ (top) and 8 kΩ (bottom) across 10 V, what is the output across the 8 kΩ?
What is the quark composition of a proton?
questions.why: Two up (+2/3 each) and one down (−1/3): total charge +1.

questions.q: In β⁻ decay, a down quark changes into…
questions.why: d → u + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ.

questions.q: Which are leptons?
questions.why: Leptons are fundamental particles that don't feel the strong force.

questions.q: An object moves in a circle of radius 2.0 m at 4.0 m s⁻¹. What is its centripetal acceleration?
Angular speed ω is related to period T by…
questions.why: One revolution is 2π radians in time T.

questions.q: If the distance between two masses doubles, the gravitational force becomes…
questions.why: F = GMm/r², an inverse-square law.

questions.q: A geostationary satellite has an orbital period of…
questions.why: It orbits above the equator, in the same direction as Earth's rotation, once every 24 hours.

questions.q: Gravitational potential at a point is…
questions.why: φ = −GM/r: work must be done to move a mass to infinity.

questions.q: What is 27 °C in kelvin?
How much energy melts 0.20 kg of ice at 0 °C? (specific latent heat of fusion 3.3 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹)
The mean kinetic energy of a molecule in an ideal gas is proportional to…
questions.why: ½m⟨c²⟩ = (3/2)kT.

questions.q: For an ideal gas, pV = …
questions.why: The ideal gas equation, with n in moles.

questions.q: The first law of thermodynamics is ΔU = q + W. W is…
questions.why: In the Cambridge convention, W is work done on the system.

questions.q: For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on…
questions.why: There are no intermolecular forces, so internal energy is all kinetic, set by temperature.

questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, acceleration is…
o: proportional to displacement and opposite in direction
questions.why: Defining equation of SHM: a = −ω²x.

questions.q: At what point of an SHM is the speed greatest?
questions.why: All the energy is kinetic at x = 0.

questions.q: What is resonance?
o: A large amplitude when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency
questions.why: Maximum energy transfer happens when the frequencies match.

questions.q: The electric field between parallel plates 0.020 m apart with 400 V across them is…
Coulomb's law: halving the distance between two charges makes the force…
questions.why: Coulomb's law is an inverse-square law: F ∝ 1/r².

questions.q: A 100 µF capacitor is charged to 12 V. How much energy is stored?
What is the time constant of a 2.0 kΩ resistor and 50 µF capacitor?
Capacitors in parallel…
questions.why: In parallel, capacitances add.

questions.q: What is the force on a 0.50 m wire carrying 3.0 A at right angles to a 0.20 T field?
A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field at right angles. Its path is…
questions.why: The force Bqv is always perpendicular to the velocity, giving circular motion.

questions.q: Lenz's law is a consequence of conservation of…
questions.why: The induced current opposes the change that caused it; otherwise energy would be created.

questions.q: A sinusoidal a.c. has a peak voltage of 325 V. What is its r.m.s. value?
What does a single diode do to a.c.?
questions.why: It lets current through in one direction only, removing half of each cycle.

questions.q: The energy of a photon is E = hf. Doubling the frequency…
questions.why: E is proportional to f.

questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of light above the threshold frequency…
o: increases the maximum kinetic energy of electrons
increases the number of electrons emitted per second
questions.why: More photons per second release more electrons; each photon still has the same energy.

questions.q: Electron diffraction is evidence that electrons…
questions.why: Diffraction is a wave property; λ = h/p.

questions.q: Binding energy per nucleon is greatest for nuclei around…
questions.why: Iron-56 is near the peak; fusion of lighter and fission of heavier nuclei both release energy.

questions.q: A source has decay constant λ. Its half-life is…
In ultrasound imaging, a gel is used between the probe and skin to…
o: reduce reflection at the air boundary (match acoustic impedance)
questions.why: Air causes almost total reflection; gel matches impedances so ultrasound enters the body.

questions.q: PET scanning detects…
o: pairs of gamma photons from positron–electron annihilation
questions.why: A positron annihilates with an electron, emitting two gamma photons in opposite directions.

questions.q: A standard candle is…
o: an object of known luminosity, used to find distances
questions.why: Knowing L and measuring the flux F gives the distance from F = L/4πd².

questions.q: Hubble's law states that the recession speed of a galaxy is proportional to…
questions.why: v = H₀d, evidence for an expanding Universe.

questions.q: Wien's displacement law: a hotter star's peak wavelength is…
questions.why: λmax ∝ 1/T, so hotter stars peak at shorter wavelengths (bluer).
